# Old South End Partnership

> The Old South End Partnership (OSE Partnership, OSEP) brings ten Toledo, Ohio organizations together so Old South End neighbors can find, keep, and strengthen the homes they love.

Last updated: 2026-10-09

## About

The Old South End Partnership exists to accelerate the renewal of Toledo’s Old South End through coordinated, data-driven, and community-led investment in housing, infrastructure, and quality of life. Ten organizations work side by side across five functions: direct housing support, land and blight, capital and gap financing, legal protection, and community anchors. After a year of planning together in 2025–2026, the partners are now carrying out a shared, multi-year plan, starting in the Pilot Zone.

- Also known as: OSE Partnership, OSEP
- Place: Old South End, Toledo, Ohio
- Formed: September 2025, by six founding partners; took its official name in February 2026
- Languages: English and Spanish
- Powered by: John Henry Eldred Jr. Foundation; Greater Toledo Community Foundation
- Website: https://www.oseptoledo.org

## How the partnership is organized

- Steering Committee: leaders of the partner organizations and funders, steering key decisions and big-picture goals.
- Pilot Project Team: day-to-day partner staff developing the projects the Steering Committee guides.
- Community Advisory Group: community voices making sure residents and stakeholders are part of the team.

## The Pilot Zone

The Old South End "Wedge" is split into zones. The partners started in the Pilot Zone, and future zones will follow. A Neighborhood Inventory looked at every property in the Pilot Zone to guide where the partners focus first.

## Key facts (as of 2026-09-25)

- 10 partner organizations
- 315 properties inventoried
- 3-year shared commitment

## Partners

- [Historic South Initiative](https://www.historicsouth.org/) (founding partner): Full remodels, new construction, and exterior repair and stabilization in the Old South End.
- [John Henry Eldred Jr. Foundation](https://www.jhefoundation.org/) (founding partner): A Northwest Ohio funder that sits alongside partners on the Steering Committee and Pilot Project Team.
- [LadderUp Housing](https://www.ladderuphousing.com/) (founding partner): Building new modular homes in the Old South End.
- [Lucas County Land Bank](https://lucascountylandbank.org/) (founding partner): Demolition, nuisance abatement, home renovation, and move-in-ready homeownership.
- [Maumee Valley Habitat for Humanity](https://mvhabitat.org/) (founding partner): Home preservation and critical repairs, plus a Financial Opportunity Center open to Old South End residents.
- [Toledo LISC](https://www.lisc.org/toledo/) (founding partner): Acquisition and rehab funding, development gap grants, and zero-interest recoverable grants for nonprofit partners.
- [The Believe Center](https://www.believecenter.org/): A trusted anchor for youth and families, offering education, mentorship, and enrichment, and helping residents navigate housing needs.
- [The Fair Housing Center](https://toledofhc.org/): Direct legal representation for residents, plus nuisance abatement, receivership, and tangled title cases.
- [Greater Toledo Community Foundation](https://toledocf.org/): A regional funder that sits alongside partners on the Steering Committee and Pilot Project Team.
- [Sofia Quintero Art & Cultural Center](https://sqacc.org/): Home of El Centro Hub and community gardens, offering bilingual, bicultural navigation, referrals, and a meeting space for partners.

## Milestones

- September 2025, Partnership formed: Six founding partners came together to start planning for the Old South End.
- November 2025, The circle grew: The Greater Toledo Community Foundation joined the effort, along with The Fair Housing Center and the Sofia Quintero Art & Cultural Center. The City of Toledo approved The Fair Housing Center as a Community Based Development Organization focused on the Old South End.
- January 2026, Set shared goals: Partners spent a full day building a shared plan for the goals and outcomes they’re working toward.
- February 2026, Became the Old South End Partnership: The coalition took its official name and formed its Steering Committee and Pilot Project Team.
- 2026, Old South End named a RISE area: The Lucas County Land Bank designated the neighborhood a Rebuild, Invest, Stabilize, and Engage area.
- March 2026, Launched the housing pilot: Partners announced their first work in the Pilot Zone at a press conference at the Sofia Quintero Art & Cultural Center.
- April 2026, Walked the neighborhood together: Led by the Lucas County Land Bank, all partners recorded conditions on 900 parcels across the Old South End. Next steps for each block will be shaped with homeowners, renters, and neighbors.
- June 2026, Largest-ever Rock the Block cleanup: Every partner volunteered at Maumee Valley Habitat for Humanity’s Rock the Block, the biggest Old South End cleanup yet.
- Summer 2026, Recognized as a Rising Community Catalyst: The Greater Toledo Community Foundation recognized Historic South Initiative and the OSE Partnership for their work revitalizing the Old South End.
- Summer 2026, New homes for Pilot Zone families: Historic South Initiative sold 2 new modular homes to Pilot Zone homeowners, LadderUp Housing poured foundations for 4 more, and Maumee Valley Habitat for Humanity completed 2 home projects.

## What's next

- Historic South Initiative: Two more new homes under construction in the Pilot Zone, plus 17 sidewalk replacements on Knower Street.
- LadderUp Housing: Foundations are poured for 4 new modular homes in the Pilot Zone, with more homes on the way.
- Lucas County Land Bank: Scheduled 8 Pilot Zone buildings for demolition, with 32 planned across the neighborhood.
- Maumee Valley Habitat for Humanity: Opened its Financial Opportunity Center with coaching opportunities for OSE residents. Five more homes are under construction.
- Toledo LISC: Gave HSI a Core City grant and an interest-free loan to buy, remodel, and sell the home at 204 South.
- The Fair Housing Center: Partnering with the Broadway Corridor Coalition and the Land Bank to bring vacant properties under receivership.
- Sofia Quintero Art & Cultural Center: Coordinating resident engagement and trust-building, and hosting partner meetings, including The Fair Housing Center’s monthly community meetings.
- The Believe Center: Helping residents navigate housing needs while continuing its youth and family programs.
